PullRequest.Title: agentHost: simplify Mission Control settings
PullRequest.Body:

Keep Mission Control's main opt-in setting and remove three implementation/testing controls from user configuration:

- `chat.agentHost.experimentalMissionControl.endpoint`
- `chat.agentHost.experimentalMissionControl.requireConnectionBinding`
- `chat.agentHost.experimentalMissionControlFakeEndpoint`

The workbench registers with the existing production default, `https://api.github.com`, only when the main setting is enabled. Preserve compatibility with deployed pre-sealed authentication tokens, including validation of supplied bindings. Backend endpoint injection, local test-server support, and mandatory-binding tests remain available through `IMissionControlOptions`; no backend authentication validation is removed.

Leftover values for the removed settings no longer redirect registration, activate test mode, require binding, or trigger reconfiguration. Update the operational documentation and add contribution-level regression tests covering the configuration registry, ignored old values, opt-in/withdrawal, empty windows, and AI-hidden withdrawal.

Follow-up to #339513. This is a separate branch from `main` and leaves #340098 unchanged.

### Validation

- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/remoteAgentHost.contribution.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/missionControlContribution.test.ts` — passed. The new test was linted again after its final fixture update.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/missionControlContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/missionControlAuthentication.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/missionControlProtocolServer.test.ts --grep 'Mission Control' --reporter dot` — passed, 81 tests.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Live Mission Control registration was not exercised; backend registration and authentication tests use injected fixtures.

(Written by Copilot)

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench restoration with Mission Control disabled (the default)
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the workbench is restored, a zero-delay scheduler reads the opt-in setting and returns. No agent-host startup, authentication lookup, IPC configuration, filesystem, database, or network work is reached, so this is off the editor startup critical path beyond the small scheduled callback.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One contribution instance per window; constant work independent of workspace folders, sessions, and accounts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: RunOnceScheduler coalesces same-tick requests and Throttler serializes configuration callbacks within the window.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is needed on the disabled path. The default remains false. The prior code additionally read the fake-endpoint setting before returning; the changed code does less work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed enabled check and complete downstream call path were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the path terminates before expensive boundaries.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Disabled startup remains boundary-free and is slightly narrower than before.

Scenarios.Scenario: Supported opt-in registration on restored workbench, including an empty window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Registration is asynchronous relative to workbench restoration, but Mission Control readiness waits for authentication session lookup, lazy agent-host startup, management IPC, GitHub identity validation, root normalization, session/policy reads, service registration, signing-key fetch, and relay connection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authentication provider getSessions, potentially activating the provider, once for the configured provider and scope set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider call per serialized configuration attempt; returned S sessions are mapped into sets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same call occurred for enabled live registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the agent host can be configured, but does not block general workbench restoration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Lazily start/connect the native Agent Host process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one process/client startup per local agent-host service lifetime; later calls are idempotent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Enabled live registration already called startAgentHost.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for Mission Control readiness, off the general restored-workbench critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send configureMissionControl over the delayed management MessagePort channel to the Agent Host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC call per serialized contribution configuration attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same management IPC was used with the configured endpoint, live flag, and optional binding flag.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each workspace root synchronously and read or atomically initialize the persisted compute identity file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: F realpathSync calls per initial configure; one identity-file read, with a bounded write/rename only when missing or relocated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same work occurred for live registration; live empty windows already permitted F=0.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs in the Agent Host before backend registration completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List the persisted session catalog to compute current_sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced list computation per check-in that needs capabilities; one catalog query plus the existing session-list computation, returning N sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same capability collection occurred on live check-in.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bounded registration work must finish before the registration request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read Copilot runtime managed settings through rpc.managedSettings.read().
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK RPC per live check-in that reaches policy collection, not per session or root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same live registration policy read occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The policy read is mandatory before registration can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate the GitHub owner, register the environment, fetch signing keys, open the Web PubSub relay, and maintain heartbeat/token refresh traffic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold successful registration performs one GitHub /user GET, one registration POST, one JWKS GET, and one persistent relay connection; steady state sends at most the scheduled heartbeat roughly once per minute plus bounded token/key refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: For the supported enabled configuration using the prior default endpoint, request count, destination, relay lifetime, and heartbeat cadence were identical.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These calls determine Mission Control readiness but are asynchronous to general workbench restoration.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One authentication/configuration attempt per coalesced trigger; F file-scheme workspace folders are normalized, S authentication sessions are inspected, and the session catalog query returns N persisted sessions. Empty windows have F=0. Network request count is constant rather than per folder or session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The contribution's Throttler serializes attempts per window; MissionControlEnvironment's Sequencer serializes process-wide configuration; same-generation check-ins are coalesced. Agent-host startup is lazy/idempotent. No new aggregate burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm agent-host configuration reuses the environment when options are compatible; signing keys are cached for five minutes, current check-ins are coalesced, and heartbeats run on a 60-second schedule. Identity/session lookups are repeated on contribution triggers as before. Empty live windows were already accepted before the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: contribution scheduling, IPC forwarding, process startup, environment sequencing, filesystem/database work, HTTP requests, relay setup, caches, and heartbeat cadence were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider activation, catalog size, filesystem latency, and network duration vary by machine/account, but the diff does not increase their cardinality on the supported opt-in path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The production default path is behaviorally and operationally equivalent; hardcoding live=true and the existing default API URL does not add work because this path is now reachable only when the main setting is true.

Scenarios.Scenario: Main opt-in changes, AI-hidden withdrawal, workspace/authentication changes, and removed-setting edits
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Enabling follows the registration path above. Disabling or hiding AI withdraws immediately and sends one management IPC; if already registered, the Agent Host may serialize one offline heartbeat. Workspace/authentication events schedule a serialized reconfiguration as before. Changes to removed settings no longer schedule or withdraw anything.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Configure or withdraw Mission Control through the management channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per serialized retained trigger when configuration proceeds; zero calls for edits to any removed setting after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Main setting, workspace, authentication, sentiment, and agent-host events already used this path; each legacy setting edit also triggered withdrawal/reconfiguration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Affects Mission Control availability, not the editor interaction critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optionally send an offline heartbeat on withdrawal, or repeat the bounded registration sequence on reconfiguration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one offline request for an established environment per sequenced withdrawal and one coalesced registration attempt on a retained update. Legacy-setting changes now cause zero requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Legacy setting changes could previously cause this network work; the diff removes that repeated-work trigger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required only for remote registration state convergence.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One coalesced update per event burst per window; authentication session events inspect only their added/removed session arrays. Multiple windows share a process-wide Sequencer in the Agent Host.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: RunOnceScheduler coalesces events, Throttler serializes per-window work, and the process-side Sequencer serializes configure/withdraw operations. This is unchanged for retained triggers; legacy setting triggers are eliminated.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The contribution retains account/session IDs to decide withdrawal and the backend retains the active environment. Withdrawal clears relay/sealing/mirror state and queues an optional offline heartbeat. Removed-setting values are now ignored rather than acting as cache/configuration keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all event handlers, coalescing primitives, withdrawal behavior, and downstream sequencing were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual event frequency and number of open windows vary, but the changed trigger set only decreases work for removed settings.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Retained triggers preserve prior costs, while edits to removed settings eliminate authentication, IPC, filesystem/database, and network reconfiguration work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Legacy configurations containing removed fake-endpoint or endpoint values
Scenarios.CriticalPath: With the main opt-in false and a stale fake endpoint, the old code could start local test registration; the changed code returns before all boundaries. With the main opt-in true and a stale fake endpoint, the old conflict check failed before authentication while the changed code performs the normal production registration path because the stale key is intentionally no longer a control.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For main-enabled configurations formerly vetoed only by a stale fake-endpoint value, start the Agent Host and execute normal production registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lazy process startup and one serialized registration lifecycle for an explicitly enabled configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The stale fake-endpoint conflict threw before authentication, process startup, IPC, filesystem/database, or network registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the now-intended Mission Control opt-in; asynchronous to general workbench restoration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the normal constant-count production identity/registration/JWKS/relay sequence for an explicitly enabled configuration whose stale fake-endpoint value is now ignored.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same cold and steady-state counts as the supported opt-in path; no scaling with the number of stale settings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old stale-value veto prevented these calls; conversely, with the main setting false a stale fake endpoint could cause local test registration, which the diff removes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines availability of the explicitly enabled feature.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A bounded migration subset: users with persisted removed keys. Work remains one registration lifecycle per explicitly enabled window, not per key/value or collection item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The same scheduler, Throttler, process Sequencer, and check-in coalescing apply. No parallel fan-out is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Removed keys are excluded from configuration registry and event invalidation. Production registration uses the existing backend caches and heartbeat lifecycle described above.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted conflict branch and the new sole opt-in check establish the before/after reachability.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of users who both opted in and retained a conflicting fake endpoint is unknown; the added lifecycle is nevertheless bounded to the explicitly enabled feature.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance finding. The only legacy edge that newly reaches expensive work has the main registration opt-in explicitly enabled, and executing that registration is the intended behavior of removing the obsolete veto; disabled users see a reduction in work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced startup, configuration events, authentication, subprocess/IPC, filesystem/database, SDK policy, HTTP, relay, heartbeat, cache, cleanup, and concurrency behavior. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and there is insufficient evidence that the cleanup of legacy reconfiguration triggers is a shipped regression fix requiring blame-based learning.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
